items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: Sam...I can't think of his name, a piano player...he had the band... He wrote that number "Stardust."

ctx.x: Very quiet and didn't have much to say. But his band... The sidemen mostly ran that band. Syndicator(?). I would still say it's a syndicator(?). If they like you, they like you. If they don't like you, they don't like you. I did very good staying as long as I did, two years.

And after that band broke up, then I come on back up in Harlem at the Victoria. I stayed there about two years. Then they decided they wanted to start to broadcast from there. So we went out about three months... No, I'd say in about six months we went out, and went on down to the Brickwood. That's right across the street from where the Savoy used to be. The Brickwood was at 140th Street and Lenox Avenue. And this guy who had the band at his studio... I think he broadcast once a week from the Victoria. Sam...I…
